translations.literal: Chunhua year 3, sixth month, day dingchou: black wind rose from the northwest; heaven and earth were dim; thunder sounded; after a while it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chunhua 3, sixth month, day dingchou: black wind rose from the northwest, the sky went dark, thunder rolled, then it ceased.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年九月，無為軍城北暴風，晝晦不可辨，拔木，壞城門、營壘、民舍。

translations.literal: Dazhong Xiangfu year 2, ninth month: violent wind north of Wuwu Army city; daytime was dark and unrecognizable; it uprooted trees and damaged city gates, camps, and common dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 2, ninth month: a violent wind north of Wuwu Army city darkened the day beyond recognition, uprooted trees, and damaged the gates, camps, and houses.

sentences.zh: 天聖六年二月庚辰，大風晝暝。

translations.literal: Tiansheng year 6, second month, day gengchen: a great wind; daytime darkened.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng 6, second month, day gengchen: a great wind darkened the day.

sentences.zh: 康定元年三月丙子，大風晝暝，經刻乃復。

translations.literal: Kangding year 1, third month, day bingzi: a great wind; daytime darkened; after several quarters it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Kangding 1, third month, day bingzi: a great wind darkened the day; after several quarters daylight returned.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年十一月丙午，大風霾。

translations.literal: Jiayou year 8, eleventh month, day bingwu: a great wind and haze.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 8, eleventh month, day bingwu: a great wind and haze.

sentences.zh: 治平二年二月乙巳，大風晝晦。

translations.literal: Zhiping year 2, second month, day yisi: a great wind; daytime was dark.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping 2, second month, day yisi: a great wind darkened the day.

sentences.zh: 四年正月庚辰朔，大風霾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, first month, first day gengchen: a great wind and haze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiping 4, first month, first day gengchen: a great wind and haze.

sentences.zh: 是日，上尊號，廷中仗衛皆不能整。

translations.literal: That day the emperor received an honorific title; in court the guard of arms bearers could not keep formation.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor received an honorific title; in court the ceremonial guard could not hold formation.

sentences.zh: 時帝已不豫，後七日崩。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was already unwell; seven days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor was already gravely ill; seven days later he died.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年四月癸亥，京師大風霾。

translations.literal: Xining year 4, fourth month, day guihai: the capital had a great wind and haze.
translations.idiomatic: Xining 4, fourth month, day guihai: a great wind haze engulfed the capital.

sentences.zh: 元祐八年二月，京師風霾。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 8, second month: wind haze at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 8, second month: wind haze at the capital.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年正月己亥，天氣昏曀，風迅發竟日。

translations.literal: Jingkang year 2, first month, day jihai: the weather was dark and murky; violent wind blew all day.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 2, first month, day jihai: the sky grew murky and dark; violent winds blew all day.

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，風霾。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingyou: wind haze.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day dingyou: wind haze.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年正月辛卯朔，大風霾。

translations.literal: Jianyan year 1, first month, first day xinmao: a great wind and haze.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan 1, first month, first day xinmao: a great wind haze.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，風霾，日色薄而有暈。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: wind haze; the sun was faint and had a halo.
translations.idiomatic: On day dingyou: wind haze; the sun was pale and ringed with a halo.

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉，汴京風霾，日無光。

translations.literal: Second month, day dingyou: wind haze at Bianjing; the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day dingyou: wind haze at Bianjing; the sun went dark.

sentences.zh: 是日，張邦昌僭位。

translations.literal: That day Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 二年七月癸未，風雨晝晦。

translations.literal: Year 2, seventh month, day guiwei: wind and rain; daytime was dark.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan 2, seventh month, day guiwei: wind and rain darkened the day.

sentences.zh: 是日，東京留守宗澤薨。

translations.literal: That day Zong Ze, the acting governor of the Eastern Capital, died.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zong Ze, acting governor of the Eastern Capital, died.

sentences.zh: 紹興十一年三月庚申，金人居長安，晝晦。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 11, third month, day gengshen: the Jin occupied Chang'an; daytime was dark.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 11, third month, day gengshen: with the Jin holding Chang'an, the day went dark.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年正月甲申，晝霾四塞。

translations.literal: Qiandao year 5, first month, day jiashen: daytime haze closed in on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 5, first month, day jiashen: daytime haze closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年​​四月丁丑，塵霾晝晦，日無光。

translations.literal: Chunxi year 5, fourth month, day dingchou: dust haze darkened the day; the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 5, fourth month, day dingchou: dust haze darkened the day and the sun went dark.

sentences.zh: 慶元九年十二月乙未，天雨霾。

translations.literal: Qingyuan year 9, twelfth month, day yiwei: the sky rained haze.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan 9, twelfth month, day yiwei: haze fell from the sky like rain.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年正月壬午，雨霾。

translations.literal: Kaixi year 1, first month, day renwu: rain haze.
translations.idiomatic: Kaixi 1, first month, day renwu: rain haze.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年正月乙未，晝霾。

translations.literal: Jiading year 10, first month, day yiwei: daytime haze.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading 10, first month, day yiwei: daytime haze.

sentences.zh: 二月癸巳，日無光。

translations.literal: Second month, day guisi: the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day guisi: the sun went dark.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年六月庚子朔，日有食之，既，天地晦冥，咫尺不辨人，雞鶩歸淒，自巳至申，其明始復。

translations.literal: Deyou year 1, sixth month, first day gengzi: there was an eclipse of the sun, total; heaven and earth were dark and dim; at arm's length one could not tell people apart; chickens and ducks returned to roost in distress; from the si hour to the shen hour, brightness only then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Deyou 1, sixth month, first day gengzi: a total solar eclipse plunged heaven and earth into darkness so deep that people a pace apart could not be told apart; chickens and ducks fled to roost in distress; from the si hour until the shen hour, daylight only then returned.

sentences.zh: 至道二年秋九月，環、慶州梨生花，佔有兵。

translations.literal: Zhidao year 2, autumn, ninth month: at Huan and Qing prefectures pear trees bore flowers; divination indicated war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao 2, autumn, ninth month: pear trees flowered at Huan and Qing prefectures—an omen of war.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹擾北邊。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan harassed the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitan raided the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 景德元年二月，保順軍城壕冰，陷起文為桃李花、雜樹、人物之狀。

translations.literal: Jingde year 1, second month: ice in the moat of Baoshun Army city sank and rose with patterns like peach and plum blossoms, miscellaneous trees, and human figures.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde 1, second month: ice in the moat of Baoshun Army city sank and heaved into patterns of peach and plum blossoms, trees, and human figures.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年正月，霸州渠冰有如華葩狀。

translations.literal: Dazhong Xiangfu year 9, first month: ice in the canal at Bazhou had shapes like flower blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 9, first month: ice in the canal at Bazhou formed blossom-like patterns.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年十月乙巳，龔丘縣檜生花，萼如蓮實。

translations.literal: Daguan year 2, tenth month, day yisi: cypress trees at Gongqiu County bore flowers; the calyxes were like lotus fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 2, tenth month, day yisi: cypress trees at Gongqiu County flowered out of season, their calyxes like lotus fruit.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年十二月，中書、門下省檢正官張宗元出撫淮西軍，寓建康。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 7, twelfth month: Zhang Zongyuan, reviewing official of the Secretariat and Chancellery, went out to oversee the Huai West army and lodged at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 7, twelfth month: Zhang Zongyuan, reviewing official of the Secretariat and Chancellery, went out to oversee the Huai West army and took lodging at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 槃冰有文如畫，佳卉茂木，華葉相敷，日易以冰，變態奇出，春暄乃止。

translations.literal: Plate ice bore patterns like paintings—fine flowers and lush trees, blossoms and leaves interwoven; each day it changed with the ice, transformations strangely emerging; it stopped only when spring warmth came.
translations.idiomatic: Plate ice bore patterns like paintings—fine flowers and lush trees, blossoms and leaves intertwined; each day the ice shifted and strange new forms appeared, until spring warmth finally ended it.

sentences.zh: 二十七年四月，徽州祁門縣圃桃已實復華。

translations.literal: Year 27, fourth month: in the garden at Qimen County, Huizhou, peach trees had already borne fruit yet flowered again.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 27, fourth month: in the garden at Qimen County, Huizhou, peach trees bore fruit and then flowered again.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，秀州呂氏家冰瓦有文，樓觀、車馬、人物、芙蓉、牡丹、萱草、藤蘿之屬，經日不釋。

translations.literal: Early Chunxi: at the Lu family home in Xiu Prefecture, ice on roof tiles bore patterns—pavilions, towers, carriages, horses, human figures, hibiscus, peonies, daylilies, wisteria, and the like—for days without clearing.
translations.idiomatic: Early Chunxi: at the Lu family home in Xiu Prefecture, ice on roof tiles bore patterns of pavilions, carriages, horses, figures, hibiscus, peonies, daylilies, and wisteria for days on end.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，興化軍仙遊縣九巫山古木末生花，臭如蘭。

translations.literal: During Chunxi: on Jiushan Mountain in Xianyou County, Xinghua Army, ancient trees bore flowers at their tips; the odor was like orchid.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi: on Jiushan Mountain in Xianyou County, Xinghua Army, ancient trees flowered at their tips with a scent like orchid.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年九月，渭南縣虸蚄蟲傷稼。

translations.literal: Jianlong year 2, ninth month: at Weinan County, locust caterpillars damaged the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong 2, ninth month: locust caterpillars damaged the crops at Weinan County.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，兗州、濟、德、磁、洺蝝生。

translations.literal: Year 3, seventh month: locust nymphs appeared at Yanzhou, Ji, De, Ci, and Ming prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong 3, seventh month: locust nymphs appeared at Yanzhou, Ji, De, Ci, and Ming prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年七月，階州虸蚄蟲生。

translations.literal: Qiande year 6, seventh month: locust caterpillars appeared at Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiande 6, seventh month: locust caterpillars appeared at Jie Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年六月，磁州青黑蟲群飛食桑，夜出晝隱，食葉殆盡。

translations.literal: Taiping Xingguo year 2, sixth month: at Cizhou, bluish-black insects flew in swarms eating mulberry; they came out at night and hid by day; they nearly devoured all the leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 2, sixth month: at Cizhou, bluish-black caterpillars swarmed the mulberry by night and hid by day until the leaves were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 七月，邢州鉅鹿、沙河二縣步屈蟲食桑麥殆盡。

translations.literal: Seventh month: at Julu and Shahe counties in Xing Prefecture, inchworm caterpillars nearly devoured all mulberry and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: inchworm caterpillars at Julu and Shahe counties in Xing Prefecture nearly stripped mulberry and wheat bare.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，濰州虸蚄蟲生，食稼殆盡。

translations.literal: Year 5, seventh month: locust caterpillars appeared at Wei Prefecture and nearly devoured all the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 5, seventh month: locust caterpillars at Wei Prefecture nearly devoured the entire harvest.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，邠州虸蚄蟲生，食稼。

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 7, ninth month: locust caterpillars at Bin Prefecture ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，泗州蠓蟲食桑。

translations.literal: Year 9, seventh month: at Sizhou, midges ate mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 9, seventh month: midges ate mulberry at Sizhou.

translations.idiomatic: Duangong 2, seventh month: locust caterpillars at Shi Prefecture damaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年四月，中都縣蜴蟲生。

translations.literal: Chunhua year 2, fourth month: locust caterpillars appeared at Zhongdu County.
translations.idiomatic: Chunhua 2, fourth month: locust caterpillars appeared at Zhongdu County.

translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: locust caterpillars at Shan Prefecture died when rain came.

translations.idiomatic: Jingde 1, eighth month: swarming insects damaged the crops at Shan, Bin, and Di prefectures.

translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 6, ninth month: locust caterpillars ate seedlings at Tong, Hua, and other prefectures in Shaanxi West.

sentences.zh: 天聖五年五月戊辰，磁州蟲食桑。

translations.literal: Tiansheng year 5, fifth month, day wuchen: insects ate mulberry at Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng 5, fifth month, day wuchen: insects ate mulberry at Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景祐四年五月，滑州靈河縣民黃慶家蠶自成被，長二丈五尺，闊四尺。

translations.literal: Jingyou year 4, fifth month: at the home of Huang Qing of Linghe County, Hua Prefecture, silkworms by themselves formed a quilt-cover, twenty-five chi long and four chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou 4, fifth month: at the home of Huang Qing of Linghe County, Hua Prefecture, silkworms spun a quilt-cover on their own, twenty-five chi long and four chi wide.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐五年，深州野蠶成繭，被於原野。

translations.literal: Jiayou year 5: wild silkworms formed cocoons and spread quilt-covers over the wild fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 5: wild silkworms formed cocoons and spread their silk across the open fields.

sentences.zh: 熙寧九年五月，荊湖南路地生黑蟲，化蛾飛去。

translations.idiomatic: Xining 9, fifth month: black insects emerged from the ground in Jinghu South Circuit, turned into moths, and flew away.

sentences.zh: 金州生黑蟲食苗，黃雀來，食之皆盡。

translations.literal: At Jin Prefecture black insects appeared eating seedlings; yellow sparrows came and ate them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Jin Prefecture black insects ate the seedlings until yellow sparrows came and devoured them all.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年閏八月，定州七縣野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Yuanyou year 6, intercalary eighth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons in seven counties of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 6, intercalary eighth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons in seven counties of Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，北海縣蠶自織如絹，成領帶。

translations.literal: Year 7, fifth month: at Beihai County silkworms wove on their own like silk and formed collar sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 7, fifth month: at Beihai County silkworms wove silk on their own into collar sashes.

sentences.zh: 元符元年七月，藁城縣野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Yuanfu year 1, seventh month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Gaocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu 1, seventh month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Gaocheng County.

sentences.zh: 八月，行唐縣野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Eighth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Xingtang County.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Xingtang County.

sentences.zh: 九月，深澤縣野蠶成繭，織紝成萬匹。

translations.literal: Ninth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Shenze County; spinning and weaving yielded ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Shenze County; spinning and weaving yielded ten thousand bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，房陵縣野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Year 2, sixth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Fangling County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu 2, sixth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Fangling County.

sentences.zh: 政和元年九月，河南府野蠶成繭。

translations.literal: Zhenghe year 1, ninth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 1, ninth month: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Henan Prefecture.

translations.literal: Year 4: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 4: wild silkworms formed cocoons at Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，南京野蠶成繭，織䌷五匹，綿四十兩，聖繭十五兩。

translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 5: wild silkworms formed cocoons at the Southern Capital; spinning yielded five bolts of silk, forty taels of floss, and fifteen taels of sacred cocoons.

translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 29, autumn: rice borers struck prefectures and counties in eastern Zhe and Jiangdong and Jiangxi.

translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 30, tenth month: rice borers and locust nymphs afflicted the Jiang and Zhe commanderies.

translations.idiomatic: Longxing 1, autumn: rice borers damaged grain across eastern and western Zhe; Shaoxing Prefecture and Huzhou suffered most.

sentences.zh: 二年，台州螟。

translations.literal: Year 2: rice borers at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing 2: rice borers at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年八月，江東郡縣螟螣。

translations.literal: Qiandao year 3, eighth month: rice borers and armyworms in Jiangdong prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 3, eighth month: rice borers and armyworms struck Jiangdong prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 淮、浙諸路多言青蟲食穀穗。

translations.literal: Many circuits along the Huai and Zhe reported green insects eating grain ears.
translations.idiomatic: Many circuits along the Huai and Zhe reported green insects eating grain ears.

translations.literal: Year 6, autumn: rice borers caused harm in western Zhe and Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 6, autumn: rice borers damaged crops in western Zhe and Jiangdong.

translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 9, autumn: rice borers at Ji and Gan prefectures, Linjiang, and Nan'an Army.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 2, autumn: rice borers struck prefectures and counties in Zhe, Jiang, and Huai.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 4, autumn: rice borers at Zhao Prefecture.

translations.literal: Year 5: Zhao Prefecture reported rice borers and armyworms.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 5: Zhao Prefecture reported rice borers and armyworms.

translations.literal: Year 7, autumn: rice borers at Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 7, autumn: rice borers at Yong Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 8, autumn: rice borers at Jiang Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 12, eighth month: at Pingjiang Prefecture insects clustered on grain ears; oil sprinkled on them made them drop at once; overnight a heavy rain washed them all away.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 14, autumn: rice borers at Jiang Prefecture and Xingguo Army.

translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 16, autumn: rice borers at Wen Prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan 3, autumn: rice borers struck Xiaoshan and Shanyin counties in eastern Zhe, Wuzhou, and Fuyang, Yanguan, Chun'an, and Yongxing counties and Jiaxing Prefecture in western Zhe.

translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan 4, autumn: insects at Qianshan County ate the grain until not an ear remained.

translations.idiomatic: Jiading 14: rice borers and armyworms brought disaster to Ming, Tai, Wen, Wu, and Qu prefectures.

translations.literal: Year 15, autumn: rice borers at Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading 15, autumn: rice borers at Gan Prefecture.

translations.literal: Year 16: rice borers at Yong and Dao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading 16: rice borers at Yong and Dao prefectures.

translations.idiomatic: Shaoding 3: rice borers at Fuzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Duanping 1, fifth month: rice borers at Dangtu County.

translations.idiomatic: Chunyou 2, fifth month: rice borers in the two Huai regions.

translations.idiomatic: Jingding 3, eighth month: rice borers in eastern and western Zhe.

translations.idiomatic: Kaibao 2: Wang Da, a commoner of Jiulong County, had a cow that bore twin calves.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，流溪縣民白延進牛生二犢。

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 3: Bai Yanjin, a commoner of Liuxi County, had a cow that bore twin calves.

sentences.zh: 五年，溫江縣民趙進牛生二犢。

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 5: Zhao Jin, a commoner of Wenjiang County, had a cow that bore twin calves.

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 6: Zhao Quan of Guangdu County had a cow that bore twin calves.

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 7: Wang Xin of Shifang County and Yuan Wu and others of Huayang County had cows that bore twin calves.

translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 8: Peng Yan of Peng Prefecture, Chen Ze of Lang Prefecture, and Wang Gongtai of Anle County had cows that bore twin calves.

translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 3: Li Zhao, a commoner of Guo Prefecture, had a cow that bore twin calves.

translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 4: Xianyu Zhi and Xianyu Gao of Qi County, Hai Luocan of Meishan County, Yin Rao of Renshou County, Li Ben of Chengdu County, and Wang Hemin of Chengji County had cows that bore twin calves.
